clue.text: The hour to be seen round about — so boring

indicators.note: to be seen round says the word for the hour wraps around the next two pieces

parts.note: an hour is a time
RE is Latin-derived crossword shorthand for about or concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds an hour hanging round them tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts RE (about) and SO inside TIME (the hour).
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome is tedious and wearying, which is what boring means.

clue.text: This is just too much for any musician!

definitions.text: This is just too much for any musician!

parts.words: This is just too much for any musician!
parts.note: the Italian score marking meaning too much, as in the instruction ma non ... (but not too much)

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads as a complaint, but it is literally a gloss: the Italian marking a musician sees on a score means too much.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction literally translates as too much, so it is the word a musician reads for excess.

clue.text: Move around or put up a collection of pictures

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word or is written upwards

parts.note: taken as written
the Tate is the London gallery holding a national art collection

explanation.surface: Someone is told to shift about or hang an exhibition of paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns OR to RO in this down entry; TATE is a famous London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn round about an axis, i.e. to move in a circle.

clue.text: It's a wrong and also right step

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of the preceding words are set out in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters of the contraction

explanation.surface: A moral puzzle: a misstep that is somehow also correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ITSA into STAI; R for right follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single step in a flight.

clue.text: Games suits

explanation.definitionFit: Sporting contests are matches; things that suit or go well together are said to match each other.

clue.text: Was responsible for a rotter being without employment

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the rotter's word sits around the employment word

parts.note: a cad is a rotter, an ungentlemanly man
employment of something is its use

explanation.surface: Blame is pinned on an unemployed scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside, so CAD goes around USE; the surface makes it mean lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To cause something is to bring it about, making you responsible for it.

clue.text: Providing tea in bars specially for the non-drinker

indicators.note: specially here means the letters are arranged in a special new way

explanation.surface: Pubs serve tea specially to cater for teetotallers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially' rearranges TEAINBARS.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer refrains from alcohol, i.e. is teetotal.

clue.text: The main way to travel cheaply

definitions.text: The main way to travel cheaply

parts.words: The main way to travel cheaply
parts.note: the main is the sea, so this means the low-cost class of passage on a ship

explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like 'principal' but is the old word for the open sea; the clue describes the cheapest accommodation on a passenger ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the lowest-fare class of passenger berth on a ship, near the rudder gear.

clue.text: Let off, as an educational institution admitted in time

indicators.note: admitted in says the school's name is let inside the word for a time

parts.note: a date is a particular time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school is let in at a set time, which sets off something.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON, the famous English boarding school, goes inside DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To let off a bomb or firework is to explode it, the sense of detonate.

clue.text: Striking girl holding a casual shirt can be worn longer

parts.note: workers on strike are out

indicators.note: holding means the girl word contains the shirt letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl
a T-shirt is a casual shirt, giving T

explanation.surface: A stunning girl wearing a T-shirt that will last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like 'attractive' but means on strike, OUT; T is from T-shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment that outlasts another survives longer, so it can be worn for more time.

clue.text: Emphasise a lock must be turned

indicators.note: must be turned says the lock word is read backwards

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Stressing that a key in a lock has to be turned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door; it is a lock of hair, TRESS, reversed to SSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert a point is to state it forcefully, putting emphasis on it.

clue.text: Disregard none with German following

indicators.note: following says the German word comes after the nought

parts.note: O is a zero, nothing at all
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: Ignoring nobody when a German comes along behind.
explanation.walkthrough: MIT is the German for 'with'; it follows O (nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to leave out or pass over, i.e. ignore.

clue.text: Strong stuff till faked

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe or cash box
sham means fake, counterfeit

explanation.surface: A powerful drink kept until a forgery is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong stuff' suggests liquor; it is a sturdy fabric. PETER is underworld slang for a safe or till.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a heavy corded ribbon or thick woollen cloth, a robust fabric.

clue.text: The man plying an oar

indicators.note: plying, working the oar back and forth, signals the letters being reworked

explanation.surface: A rower at work on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plying' rearranges ANOAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron is a male first name, the biblical brother of Moses.

clue.text: Excellent written matter and designs

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: Praising fine prose and its plans.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, 'first-class', is written AI with the digit as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aims are intentions or goals, the sense of designs as plans.

clue.text: One bearing with short weight, though cross

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
N, north, is a compass bearing
terse means short, curt
ct is the abbreviation for carat, a weight for gems

explanation.surface: Someone carrying a little weight is nonetheless annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but is the verb meaning go across.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or roads that intersect cut across one another.

clue.text: Close in spirit after this day

indicators.note: in places the closeness word inside the drink

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
nigh is an old word for near or close

explanation.surface: Feeling close in spirit once the day is over.
explanation.walkthrough: NIGH goes inside TOT, a small dram of whisky or rum.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is the evening that follows today.

clue.text: Values jennies?

explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate; a jenny is a female donkey, jokily an ass-ess, so several are ass-esses.

clue.text: Swindle is trivial for the conscience-stricken

parts.note: a con is a swindle
trite means hackneyed and trivial

explanation.surface: A small fraud leaves its perpetrator feeling guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone contrite feels remorse for a wrong, i.e. a guilty conscience.

clue.text: Boldly misbehaving lout content in beastly accommodation

indicators.note: content in means the rearranged lout is what the pig's home contains

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, home for beasts

indicators.note: misbehaving signals the letters of lout running riot

explanation.surface: A badly behaved yob is fearlessly happy in a pigsty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges LOUT to OUTL, which 'content in' places in STY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something stoutly means doing it bravely and resolutely.

clue.text: The end of many a sailors tale

indicators.note: the end of means take the final letter of many

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, sailors collectively

explanation.surface: Most sailors finish with a long story.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a long rambling story, especially one told by a seafarer.

clue.text: Fashion to order

explanation.definitionFit: To fashion or arrange something into shape is to sort it; to sort is also to put in order or classify.

clue.text: Using tapes in turn is wise

indicators.note: turn signals the letters being turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Using recording tapes one after another is sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges TAPESIN; 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient means sagacious, having great discernment.

clue.text: Exercise a top man gets in the city

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
a king is the man at the top

explanation.surface: A leader takes his exercise in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Peking is the older name for Beijing.
explanation.definitionFit: Peking is the former Western name of Beijing, China's capital.

clue.text: An avenue where a little cypress tree takes the eye

indicators.note: a little says only a small portion of the next words is taken

explanation.surface: A small cypress catches the eye down a tree-lined road.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'cypresS TREE Takes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a town road, as is an avenue.

clue.text: Register possibly ten letters for the queen

indicators.note: possibly says the word ten is one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, are the queen's letters

explanation.surface: Ten letters may be logged for Her Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TEN to ENT; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter details is to record them, to register them in a list.

clue.text: Military personnel here serve as an example

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
someone here is present

explanation.surface: Soldiers on site serve as a model for others.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent a class is to typify it, to stand as a specimen of it.

clue.text: Re-tax crooked characters more

indicators.note: crooked suggests the letters are bent out of their order

explanation.surface: Dishonest people taxing again for additional money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges RETAX.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, over and above.

clue.text: The band about to secure a harpsichord

indicators.note: about means the band word goes around the fastening word

parts.note: a set is a band or group
to pin something is to secure it

explanation.surface: A group is about to grab a keyboard instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the point of' before 'to secure'; it puts SET around PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinet is a small keyboard instrument of the harpsichord family.

clue.text: Mount really first-class horse

parts.note: the best is the finest, truly first-class
to horse someone is to set them on horseback, to give them a ride

explanation.surface: Getting on a top-quality horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride a horse is to sit astride it, mounting it.

clue.text: Has the essentials to make a case

indicators.note: the words given are only the raw ingredients, to be rearranged to make the answer

explanation.surface: The basic items needed to build a box.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HAS THE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting cover, as for a sword or knife.

clue.text: Honest but cunning backing is in view

indicators.note: is in means the turned craftiness word sits inside the view word

parts.note: a sight is a view

indicators.note: backing means the cunning word goes backwards

parts.note: art can mean craft or cunning

explanation.surface: Sincere, though sly support can be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ART to TRA, which 'is in' puts inside SIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight person is upright and truthful.
